epic_title: Resolve, create, open and navigate periodic notes
summary: NOTE owns the full lifecycle of a periodic note: knowing whether it exists, creating it (folder, template, file) when it does not, opening it the way the user asked, telling whether an arbitrary file is one of them, finding its neighbours, and keeping a fast index of all of it correct as the vault changes. FMT supplies date-to-filename and filename-to-date conversion and week/locale rules; TPL supplies what a template's tokens expand to; CAL and CMD decide when a note operation gets triggered (a click, a command, startup) and NOTE only supplies what happens once that decision is made; SET supplies the resolved folder/format/template values NOTE consumes.

stories.title: Look up whether a period already has a note
stories.story: As someone reviewing my periodic notes, I want to check whether a note for a specific day, week, month, or year already exists, so that other features can decide whether to open it or create it without guessing.
stories.rationale: Every open-or-create flow, calendar dot, and adjacent-note search depends on this lookup being fast and correct.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note exists for the requested period
acceptance_criteria.when: the lookup runs for that period
then: the existing note's file is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: no note exists for the requested period
acceptance_criteria.when: the lookup runs for that period
then: the lookup reports nothing found
no note is created as a side effect of looking
no error is thrown

acceptance_criteria.given: two moments that fall on the same day, week, month, or year but differ only in time of day
acceptance_criteria.when: the lookup runs for either moment
then: both return the same note

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity outside the release set of day, week, month, and year (quarter is reserved and not enabled, per DEC-23)
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup is requested for it
then: the error names the requested granularity and says it is not supported in this release
no file is returned

decisions.title: The first release supports day, week, month and year; quarter is reserved
decisions.decision: The set of granularities the first release supports is day, week, month and year. Quarter is a reserved value: the type may name it and configuration may round-trip it, but no command is generated for it, no note is created for it, and no view offers it. Anything asking for quarter behaves the same way as any other granularity that is not enabled.
decisions.rationale: ARCH called quarter supported, NOTE used it as the example of an unsupported granularity, ICE-01 deferred it, and CMD still listed it for generated commands and startup opening. An agent reading the backlog could not tell whether quarter paths must work. This vault has quarter disabled, so nothing is lost by reserving it.

stories.title: Enumerate every note of a granularity
stories.story: As someone auditing my notes, I want to list every note of a given granularity that exists in the vault, so that calendars, dashboards, and migrations can be built on a complete set instead of a partial guess.
stories.rationale: Calendar dots, related-note lists, and index rebuilding all need the complete set, not a sample.

acceptance_criteria.given: notes exist at several dates for a granularity, including some nested in subfolders under its configured folder
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: every one of them is returned, including the nested ones

acceptance_criteria.given: the granularity's configured folder does not exist in the vault
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: a clear error is reported naming the missing folder, instead of an empty list that looks like there are simply no notes yet

acceptance_criteria.given: the granularity's configured folder exists but is empty
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: an empty list is returned without an error

acceptance_criteria.given: a file in the configured folder does not match the granularity's configured filename format
acceptance_criteria.when: notes of that granularity are enumerated
then: that file is excluded from the results

stories.title: Resolve the folder for a note and create missing parent folders
stories.story: As someone who has never manually created a folder for my notes, I want the plugin to create whatever folders a new note needs, so that turning on a granularity or pointing it at a new folder just works without a manual setup step.
stories.rationale: A missing folder should never be the reason a note fails to be created.

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity's configured folder does not exist yet
acceptance_criteria.when: a note is created for that granularity
then: the folder, and any missing parent folders above it, are created automatically before the note is written
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts > writes the note even though the whole folder chain was missing (AC-NOTE-03.1, AC-NOTE-03.4) / > creates the missing target folder before creating the file / > accepts a folder another actor created between the check and the call (AC-NOTE-03.1) -- the last one covers the create-race the review round found.

acceptance_criteria.given: no folder is configured for a granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: the path for its note is resolved
then: the note falls back to Obsidian's own default location for new notes, rather than an unpredictable or empty path
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteUtils.test.ts > falls back to Obsidian default new-file folder when none is configured (AC-NOTE-03.2) / > resolves to the vault root when neither the config nor Obsidian names a folder (AC-NOTE-03.2) / > takes the default folder only when the config names no folder at all (AC-NOTE-03.2).

acceptance_criteria.given: a configured folder path that is empty or the vault root
acceptance_criteria.when: the folder path is checked for validity
then: it is accepted as valid
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteUtils.test.ts > accepts an empty configured folder as valid and already present (AC-NOTE-03.3) / > accepts the vault root written as a slash as valid and already present (AC-NOTE-03.3) / > keeps an explicit "/" as the vault root instead of taking the default folder (AC-NOTE-03.3); plus src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts > creates no folder for a note at the vault root (AC-NOTE-03.3).

acceptance_criteria.given: a configured folder path that does not currently exist in the vault
acceptance_criteria.when: the folder path is checked for validity ahead of note creation
then: it is flagged as not-yet-created
the flag does not block a note from being created later, since the folder is made automatically at creation time
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteUtils.test.ts > flags a folder that does not exist yet as valid but not-yet-created (AC-NOTE-03.4) for the flag itself, and src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts > writes the note even though the whole folder chain was missing for the clause that the flag must not block creation. No settings-UI surface consumes the flag yet: US-SET-04 owns that wiring, which the review round confirmed as the correct scope split.

acceptance_criteria.given: a configured folder several levels deep where none of the intermediate segments exist
acceptance_criteria.when: a note is created for that granularity
then: every missing intermediate folder is created, not only the immediate parent
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts > creates every missing intermediate folder, top down (AC-NOTE-03.5) / > creates only the intermediate folders that are still missing (AC-NOTE-03.5) / > does not mistake a file for an existing folder in the chain / > refuses a path with an unusable segment before making any folder.

stories.title: Create the note for any supported granularity, reliably
stories.story: As someone keeping a periodic journal, I want creating a note to work the same reliable way for every granularity Calendaric supports, so that switching between daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly notes never surprises me with a create that silently does nothing or crashes.
stories.rationale: The old code has three different, inconsistent answers for what happens when a create goes wrong; users need one predictable answer.

acceptance_criteria.given: no note exists yet for the requested period
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested for that period
then: a new note file is written at the resolved folder and filename for that granularity
the created file is returned to the caller

acceptance_criteria.given: any two granularities from the release set of day, week, month, and year
acceptance_criteria.when: a note is created for each, under the same circumstances
then: both creations apply the same collision behaviour when a file already exists at the target path
both creations apply the same error behaviour when something goes wrong

acceptance_criteria.given: a granularity outside the release set of day, week, month, and year (quarter is reserved and not enabled, per DEC-23)
acceptance_criteria.when: a note creation is requested for it
then: the error names the requested granularity and says it is not supported in this release
no file is created

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured folder for the granularity does not exist yet
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested
then: the note is still created successfully
the missing folder is created automatically first

acceptance_criteria.given: a file already exists at the exact path a new note for this period would be written to
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested for that period
then: no existing content is overwritten or deleted
the operation reports clearly that a note already exists there, instead of silently doing nothing or throwing an unhandled error
the caller can use that report to open the existing note instead

acceptance_criteria.given: the exact path a new note would occupy is taken by something that is not a markdown note (for example a folder)
acceptance_criteria.when: a create is requested for that period
then: the error names the occupied path and says it is not a Markdown note
nothing at that path is altered or deleted

decisions.title: Opening and creating a note share one entry point
decisions.decision: Every caller goes through open-or-create, which checks existence first. There is no separate create path that skips that check.
decisions.rationale: Two entry points means two places where the file-already-exists case can be handled differently, which is how the old code ended up with three different answers to the same question.

stories.title: Apply the configured template when creating a note
stories.story: As someone with a note-taking routine, I want each newly created periodic note to start from my configured template, so that I do not have to add the same headings and frontmatter by hand every time.
stories.rationale: A template is the difference between a useful note and a blank file; it must apply every time a note is created, not just sometimes.

acceptance_criteria.given: a template is configured for the granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: a new note is created
then: the template's content, with its tokens expanded, becomes the new note's initial content

acceptance_criteria.given: no template is configured for the granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: a new note is created
then: the note is created with empty content rather than failing

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured template file cannot be found
acceptance_criteria.when: a new note is created
then: the note is still created, with empty content
a specific, visible warning tells the user the template could not be read

acceptance_criteria.given: a saved fold state exists for the configured template
acceptance_criteria.when: a new note is created from it
then: that fold state is applied to the new note

stories.title: Open a note in the active pane, a new tab, or a split
stories.story: As someone jumping between notes quickly, I want opening a note to reuse my current view by default but let me force a new tab or a split when I ask for it, so that navigating never fights the layout I already have open.
stories.rationale: Where a note opens is as much a part of the experience as whether it opens at all.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is opened without any modifier key held
acceptance_criteria.when: it opens
then: it reuses the current unpinned tab instead of opening a new one
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts > AC-NOTE-06.1: reuses the current unpinned tab on a plain click / > AC-NOTE-06.1: reuses the current tab on a Ctrl click on macOS; plus src/adapters/obsidianWorkspaceAdapter.test.ts > AC-NOTE-06.1: asks for the active leaf so the current unpinned tab is reused. Reuse goes through getLeaf(false), which Obsidian own typings name as the replacement for the deprecated getUnpinnedLeaf. Whether the reused tab is the one the user perceives as active needs a live host.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is opened while the platform's split modifier key (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) is held
acceptance_criteria.when: it opens
then: it opens in a split next to the current view instead of replacing it
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts > isSplitModifierPressed (AC-NOTE-06.2) suite, including > AC-NOTE-06.2: opens a split on a Cmd click on macOS and > AC-NOTE-06.2: opens a split on a Ctrl click off macOS; plus the adapter test > AC-NOTE-06.2: asks for a split leaf. The platform split matters: a first implementation treated Ctrl and Meta as equivalent everywhere, so a macOS Ctrl-click wrongly split -- both platforms are now asserted separately rather than against one mocked platform.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is opened as part of the startup flow rather than a direct user click
acceptance_criteria.when: it opens
then: it opens in a new tab rather than reusing or replacing whatever tab is already active
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts > AC-NOTE-06.3: opens a new tab instead of reusing the active one, plus the adapter test > AC-NOTE-06.3: asks for a tab leaf. PARTIAL, reported rather than judged complete: the criterion says as part of the STARTUP FLOW, and that call sits in src/main.ts, which has no test harness and which five other live branches own -- so the tab-versus-reuse decision is proven while the startup wiring itself is unverified and needs a live host.

acceptance_criteria.given: the resolved file was deleted or moved between being found and being opened
acceptance_criteria.when: opening it is attempted
then: a notice says that the file could not be opened because it no longer exists at the resolved path
no unrelated file is opened in its place
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/adapters/obsidianWorkspaceAdapter.test.ts > AC-NOTE-06.4 suite -- reports the file as missing when the path no longer resolves / claims no leaf and opens nothing / opens nothing when an unrelated file has taken over the path / opens nothing when the note moved away and another file took its old path / opens nothing when a folder now occupies the path; plus src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts > AC-NOTE-06.4: reports that the file no longer exists at the resolved path. Three review rounds went into this one criterion: it first followed a moved file to its new location, which satisfied the no-unrelated-file clause but not the notice clause, and the wrappers rebuilt the path from the mutable file.path so a retained handle escaped the check. foundAtPath is now a required parameter carrying the immutable looked-up path, so no call site can reintroduce that silently. Honest limits: the criterion is testable_by integration, so Obsidian own object-identity and path-mutation behaviour, and the Notice actually appearing, remain unobserved here.

stories.title: Activating a period opens or creates its note
stories.story: As someone keeping a periodic journal, I want activating a period to take me straight to its note, so that I never have to manually find or create the file myself.
stories.rationale: This is the single most-used operation in the plugin: the payoff every other NOTE story exists to support.

acceptance_criteria.given: no note exists for the activated period
acceptance_criteria.when: that period is activated
then: a note is created for it
the newly created note opens

acceptance_criteria.given: a note already exists for the activated period
acceptance_criteria.when: that period is activated
then: the existing note opens
no duplicate is created and its content is left unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the setting to confirm before creating is turned on and no note exists for the activated period
acceptance_criteria.when: that period is activated
then: the user is asked to confirm before any file is written
declining the confirmation creates nothing and opens nothing

acceptance_criteria.given: the setting to confirm before creating is turned off and no note exists for the activated period
acceptance_criteria.when: that period is activated
then: the note is created and opened immediately, without any prompt

acceptance_criteria.given: creating the note for the activated period fails
acceptance_criteria.when: that period is activated
then: the error names the period and says the note could not be created
no blank or broken pane is left open in place of a real note

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing weekly note file named in the pretty format (for example "2025-W46, 10.11 - 16.11.md") and prefix matching enabled for the weekly format
acceptance_criteria.when: that week is activated
then: the existing pretty-named file opens
no raw-named duplicate file (for example "2025-W46.md") is created

stories.title: Know whether a file is a periodic note, and which period
stories.story: As someone who wants navigation commands to only apply where they make sense, I want the plugin to tell whether any given file is one of my periodic notes and, if so, which period it represents, so that features like jump-to-adjacent only ever activate for real periodic notes.
stories.rationale: Every command that only makes sense on a periodic note needs a precise, folder-scoped answer to 'is this one?'.

acceptance_criteria.given: a file sits inside a granularity's configured folder and matches its configured format
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is checked
then: it is recognised as a periodic note of that granularity
the exact period it represents is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: a file's name looks like a date but the file does not live inside any granularity's configured folder
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is checked
then: it is not recognised as a periodic note

acceptance_criteria.given: a file is not a markdown file
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is checked
then: it is never recognised as a periodic note, regardless of its name

acceptance_criteria.given: a file was previously recognised as a period's note and is then renamed without changing which period it represents
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is checked again
then: it is still recognised as the same period's note

stories.title: Find the closest existing adjacent note
stories.story: As someone reviewing my history, I want to jump to the closest existing note before or after the one I am looking at, without creating anything new, so that I can browse what I have actually written without accidentally adding empty notes.
stories.rationale: Browsing history and filling in a missing day are two different intents and must not be conflated.

acceptance_criteria.given: at least one earlier note and one later note of the same granularity exist relative to a reference note
acceptance_criteria.when: the previous, or the next, adjacent note is requested
then: the nearest existing note in that direction is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: no earlier, or no later, note of that granularity exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the previous, or the next, adjacent note is requested in the direction with nothing there
then: nothing is returned, instead of an error or a result wrapped around to the other end

acceptance_criteria.given: the reference file is not itself a recognised periodic note
acceptance_criteria.when: an adjacent note is requested from it
then: nothing is returned, since there is no period to be adjacent to

acceptance_criteria.given: the neighbouring date for the requested direction has no note yet
acceptance_criteria.when: the closest existing adjacent note is requested
then: no note is created for that neighbouring date
finding an existing neighbour and creating the note for a specific neighbouring date remain two separate operations

stories.title: Template a manually created file that matches note settings
stories.story: As someone who creates note files by hand, I want an empty file whose folder and filename match a configured periodic-note folder and format to receive the configured template, so that manually created notes match notes created by Calendaric.
stories.rationale: A note's origin should not change what it looks like once it is recognised as a period's note.

acceptance_criteria.given: Calendaric is already running and a new, completely empty file is created directly in a granularity's configured folder with a name matching its configured format, whether created by Calendaric itself, the user, or another plugin
acceptance_criteria.when: that file is resolved
then: the configured template is applied to it, regardless of which of those created it

acceptance_criteria.given: the manually created file already has content
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is resolved
then: no template is applied
the existing content is left untouched

acceptance_criteria.given: an empty file whose folder and filename match a configured periodic-note folder and format already existed before Calendaric first started
acceptance_criteria.when: that startup lookup resolves the file
then: the template is not retroactively applied to it
the file is left untouched

decisions.title: Leave matching files unchanged at startup; template later arrivals
decisions.decision: A matching empty file found while the index is first built is indexed and left untouched. A matching empty file that appears while Calendaric is running is templated, whoever created it: Calendaric itself, the user, or another plugin.
decisions.rationale: A matching file has a folder and filename that match a configured periodic-note folder and format. The line is drawn at startup, not at authorship. Templating everything found at startup would write into files the plugin has never seen, as a side effect of installing it. Refusing to template anything the user creates by hand would break the ordinary case of making tomorrow's note in the file explorer and expecting the template to fill it.

stories.title: Keep periodic-note lookup current as vault files change
stories.story: As someone who relies on instant calendar dots, jump commands, and open-or-create decisions, I want the plugin to always know instantly which files are my periodic notes without rescanning the whole vault every time, so that every other periodic-note feature stays fast and correct as I create, rename, or delete files.
stories.rationale: Every other NOTE story depends on this lookup staying correct as files change; if it drifts from reality, all of them silently break.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin starts and files already exist in the vault that match a granularity's configured folder and format
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup runs for one of those files' periods
then: the matching file is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: a new file is created that matches a granularity's configured folder and format
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup runs for that file's period straight after
then: the newly created file is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: a file that a lookup already returns for its period is renamed to a different name that still matches its granularity's configured folder and format, including being renamed by an external script from a raw title to a longer 'pretty' title
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup runs for that period after the rename completes
then: the file is returned under its new name

acceptance_criteria.given: a file's name happens to match a granularity's configured format but the file lives outside every granularity's configured folder
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup runs for the period its name would suggest
then: nothing is returned for that file

acceptance_criteria.given: a plugin setting that affects which files count as periodic (for example a folder or a format) is changed
acceptance_criteria.when: the change is saved
then: a lookup made after the change reflects the new configuration
a file that only matches under the new settings is now returned by a lookup for its period
a file that no longer matches is no longer returned by any lookup

acceptance_criteria.given: a file carries a periodic date in its frontmatter and lives inside that granularity's configured folder
acceptance_criteria.when: a lookup runs for that period
then: the file is returned even if its filename alone would not have matched

acceptance_criteria.given: a file that a lookup previously returned for its period is deleted
acceptance_criteria.when: the deletion is noticed
then: a lookup for that period afterwards returns nothing
the calendar dot for that day disappears

notes: Every 'build' uid assigned to NOTE is covered by exactly one story's covers[]; none were left in uncovered[].

The generic create-note dispatcher's real defect (missing quarter/year branches, dni:create-periodic-note) is addressed as AC-NOTE-04.2/.3 rather than narrated as a bug: the entry point must handle every granularity Calendaric supports and report a clear error for one it does not.

Existing-file handling (AC-NOTE-04.5/.6) picks one answer where the old code had three (dni swallows the error behind a generic Notice and resolves undefined; pn lets vault.create's exception propagate unhandled; neither tells the caller anything actionable). The chosen answer: report the conflict clearly enough that the caller (typically US-NOTE-07's open-or-create) can recover by opening the existing note, and never destroy what is already on disk.

The vault-wide loose date-fallback (pn:loose-date-parsing-fallback-global) is icebox and intentionally excluded; AC-NOTE-08.2 and AC-NOTE-11.4 instead require folder-scoping as the only way a file is recognised as periodic.

Several stories (US-NOTE-03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11) are marked granularity-agnostic (day/week/month/year) even though Calendaric's own current code only wires day and week end-to-end; the underlying behaviour is already granularity-generic in the prior-art libraries (dni, pn), and quarter is reserved and out of scope for this release, per DEC-23. Wiring month/year all the way through settings UI and the calendar grid is CAL/SET/CMD/TPL's job, not NOTE's.

Most acceptance criteria are testable_by unit against a pre-populated index/cache and mocked vault calls; anything that touches a real Obsidian workspace leaf, a real vault.createFolder, or the confirmation modal is marked integration or (for the modal's own prompt) manual, since this epic's tests will need a fuller Obsidian mock (TFile, Vault, Workspace, MetadataCache) than exists in the current test suite.

pn:jump-to-adjacent-note-command and pn:open-adjacent-note-command are epic CMD, not NOTE: CMD's commands compose US-NOTE-09's closest-existing lookup and US-NOTE-07's open-or-create to implement 'jump to closest existing' and 'open the neighbouring date, creating it if needed' respectively. NOTE supplies both underlying operations; CMD decides how a command palette entry uses them.
